key_insight: There is no single best model or decoding setting that reliably produces the most comprehensive set of valid answers; instead, learning a router that selects among models or sampling strategies per prompt maximizes the coverage of unique high-quality responses.
problem_solved: How to elicit a comprehensive, diverse set of valid answers for prompts that admit many correct responses, overcoming limits of any single model or fixed sampling strategy.
method: Define a new evaluation metric, diversity coverage, that scores the total quality of unique answers relative to an optimal set of the same size.
Train a learned router to select among multiple models and/or sampling configurations per prompt so the assembled output set maximizes diversity coverage.
Use an ensemble of complementary models or decoding strategies and optimize routing decisions (via supervised/meta learning or reward-guided training) to produce more unique high-quality responses.
impact: Practitioners can generate more comprehensive and useful answer sets by routing requests to the right model/strategy, improving user satisfaction in tasks where many valid outputs exist (e.g., creative generation, question answering, dialog). This enables modular systems that trade off quality and novelty more effectively.
visual_elements: Schematic: input prompt -> learned router -> multiple models/sampling strategies -> aggregated unique answers (shows routing decisions)
Bar chart: diversity coverage comparison (single best model vs. router-based ensemble) across prompt types
Before/After example: one prompt with a single-model output vs. router outputs showing multiple distinct valid answers
Flowchart: training loop for the router (metric evaluation -> routing update -> model outputs)
paper_title: No Single Best Model for Diversity: Learning a Router for Sample Diversity
paper_authors: Yuhan Liu, Fangyuan Xu, Vishakh Padmakumar, Daphne Ippolito, Eunsol Choi
